scope: Fork-only feasibility of the complete Rust x64 release on a standard GitHub-hosted Windows runner, not a storage comparison
source_amendment: Pin the current PR head, including review feedback, rather than the older fork merge. Apply only the previously recorded bootstrap-runtime-probe.patch so the configured Clang probe executes in bootstrap dry-run mode. Record both the patch digest and applied diff. Do not change the PR's PGO implementation, training scenarios, parallelism, optimization flags, tools or artifact tests.
runner: windows-2025, public GitHub-hosted, exactly four logical processors; record actual CPU, RAM, image and storage without choosing a CPU vendor or disk bus
storage: Stock NTFS. Use D:\rust-src and D:\compiler-cache. No partitioning, ReFS, Defender, paging or temporary-directory changes.
cache_handoff_amendment: Run40140100420 completed both PGO stages but timed out during final LLVM compilation. Job Object termination worked; the subsequent unconditional sccache --stop-server failed because the server was already dead, incorrectly preventing cache upload and the restored attempt. For a recorded timeout with exit124, the command and its server are already terminated, so preserve the on-disk cache without stopping it again. Normal completion still requires a successful server stop. Validate this path with a real hosted sccache timeout, artifact upload from a failed job and download on a fresh VM before repeating the full attempt. The original cache was not uploaded and cannot be recovered.

attempts.condition: Empty local compiler cache and fresh source/build/profile directories
attempts.follow_up: After success or failure, stop sccache and preserve its available entries. A partial cache is allowed and is not described as fully warm.

attempts.condition: Fresh VM and source checkout. Restore only this run's cold-attempt compiler-cache artifact; no build outputs, PGO profiles, source workspace or upstream S3 cache.
attempts.follow_up: Run only when the cold attempt saved a compiler-cache artifact, even if that attempt timed out. Repeat the entire PGO training, full distribution and upstream artifact tests.

measurement: The 360-minute GitHub job ceiling remains unchanged. Record time from the first step and subtract all setup/cache restoration from the release budget. Reserve ten minutes after the cold attempt for cache/evidence transfer and five after the restored attempt. Record the full release command, successful phase milestones, qualification, cache statistics and API job/step times separately. A timeout at the shorter evidence-preserving deadline does not prove that completion within 360 minutes is impossible.
qualification: Require zero release exit status, no timeout, successful Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 5 and Run tests sections, complete distribution manifest, nonempty PGO profiles and native execution using the extracted compiler. Independently confirm actual whole-job duration below 360 minutes from GitHub's job metadata. MSI installation is not tested.
decision: A qualified completed cold attempt demonstrates cold feasibility for that observed runner. A qualified completed restored attempt demonstrates only compiler-cache-dependent feasibility. One success is an existence proof, not a reliable cross-hardware completion guarantee or a median. Failure or timeout of both attempts leaves standard-runner feasibility unconfirmed; do not extrapolate completion times or silently split work across jobs.
